column1: # Dash-punctuation glyph inventory — the closed set of Unicode General_
# Category=Pd (Dash_Punctuation) code points, used to fix a confirmed
# trailing/leading punctuation off an accumulated word buffer with a raw
# `char::is_ascii_punctuation()` check, which is FALSE for every non-ASCII
# Unicode dash — so real U.S. Code legal text carrying an EM DASH after a
# defining verb (`the term "developmental disability" means—` followed by
# an enumerated list, a common USC drafting convention) left the malformed
# token `means—` in the stream, which then failed lexicon lookup for the
# bare word `means`, breaking downstream grammar parsing. This table is the
# loaded, cited fix: every Pd code point, queried instead of the raw ASCII
# Source: Unicode Standard Annex #44 (Unicode Character Database), the
# General_Category property, as tabulated in the UCD's
# reference table; independently re-fetched and cross-checked row-for-row
# against the primary UCD source before this file was authored — all 25
# General_Category=Pd (Dash_Punctuation) is a SINGLE, small, closed set: 25
# code points total, none of which pair or nest (unlike Pi/Pf quotation
# marks — see `quote-glyphs.tsv`), so every row plays the identical "Dash"
# role for tokenization purposes and no role/pairing column is needed.
#   glyph       the literal UTF-8 character (for human sight-verification
#               against `codepoint`; the loader cross-checks the two agree).
#   name        the UCD character name, verbatim, for citation traceability.
